da-false-claim.evidence: topological-mass-eigenspace-decomp.md:10-20 m(ϱ) = ‖MI∫ τ̂ₙ(α)‖ + ‖MI∫(α−τ̂ₙ(α))‖, justified (in the proof sibling) by ‖α‖² = ‖τ̂ₙ(α)‖² + ‖α−τ̂ₙ(α)‖²
da-false-claim.notes: The lemma asserts a LINEAR sum of norms m = ‖A‖ + ‖B‖ where A = MI∫τ̂ₙ(α), B = MI∫(α−τ̂ₙ(α)), but the only orthogonality available (Killing-form, idempotent τ̂ₙ) gives the Pythagorean identity ‖α‖² = ‖τ̂ₙα‖² + ‖α−τ̂ₙα‖², i.e. m = √(‖A‖²+‖B‖²). For A,B ≠ 0 one has √(a²+b²) < a+b, so the stated equality is false except in the degenerate single-nonzero case. (The proof sibling even compounds this by mapping the L2-orthogonal additivity onto a multiplicative-integral PRODUCT, then claiming the product's norm is the sum of norms.)

da-vacuous.notes: The .md lemma makes a substantive (and, per da-false-claim, over-strong) normed claim — not vacuous. (The Lean sibling is separately weak; see da-lean-narrative-divergence.)

da-circular.notes: No assumption of the conclusion; the decomposition is derived from descent-eigenspace orthogonality.

da-overclaim.evidence: .md:6-8 'multiplicative-integral additivity over orthogonal direct sums gives' the linear sum identity
da-overclaim.notes: Even setting aside the L1/L2 issue, the lemma asserts that the nonabelian multiplicative integral is additive over orthogonal direct sums in a way that yields ‖∫(A⊕B)‖ = ‖∫A‖ + ‖∫B‖. The nonabelian MI is multiplicative (group-valued, see the proof sibling eq:mi-decomp which correctly writes a PRODUCT), so 'additivity → sum of norms' overclaims: the genuine content is at best ‖∫α‖ ≤ ‖∫τα‖·‖∫(α−τα)‖ submultiplicativity, which does not give an equality of sum-of-norms.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: .md:3-8: 'Killing-form orthogonality ... together with multiplicative-integral additivity ... gives' the linear normed identity (proof sibling derives ‖α‖²=‖τα‖²+‖α−τα‖² then jumps to m=‖∫τα‖+‖∫(α−τα)‖)
da-non-sequitur.notes: The inference from (a) L2 Pythagorean orthogonality and (b) MI multiplicativity to (c) a LINEAR sum of norms of the two integrals is a non-sequitur: neither premise supplies ‖A‖+‖B‖. The proof sibling's chain (lines 28-66) explicitly states the L2 identity, then a multiplicative product MI∫, then 'taking norms ... using submultiplicativity (which is an equality for the orthogonal decomposition of an idempotent)' — the parenthetical is the unjustified leap converting a product/L2 structure into an L1 sum.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.evidence: topological-mass-eigenspace-decomp.lean:44-54 tm_eigenspace_decomp proves only x = descendedPart n x + transientPart n x := JetChain.decomposition; JetProlongation.lean:155-158 decomposition := by simp [descendedPart, transientPart] where transientPart n x := x − τ̂ₙ x
da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: The Lean theorem proves the TRIVIAL identity x = τ̂ₙ(x) + (x − τ̂ₙ(x)), which holds for ANY function τ̂ₙ (the simp proof uses no orthogonality, no norm, no multiplicative integral). The .md lemma's actual content — the NORMED equality m(ϱ) = ‖MI∫τ̂ₙα‖ + ‖MI∫(α−τ̂ₙα)‖ from Killing-form orthogonality + MI additivity — is entirely absent from Lean. The Lean sibling proves a strictly weaker (and tautological) statement than the .md claims; proof-statement-integrity fails.

da-citation-misuse.evidence: .ts:15 cites yekutieli2015; proof sibling .md:38 invokes '[Proposition 5.3, yekutieli2015]' for 'additivity of the nonabelian multiplicative integral over orthogonal direct sums'
da-citation-misuse.notes: Yekutieli's nonabelian multiplicative integral is multiplicative (group-valued), not additive over direct sums; attributing a sum-of-norms additivity to a specific Yekutieli proposition is a likely misattribution of the cited result's actual content (the genuine Yekutieli statement gives a product, as the proof's own eq:mi-decomp shows). Cannot verify Prop 5.3's exact wording here, so warn.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: .md:2 integrand α=(∇_A q, L∧F⁺); .md:6-7 ‖·‖ Killing-form norm but applied to a group-valued MI∫ output
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: The norm ‖·‖ is introduced as the Killing-form norm on su(2) (a Lie-ALGEBRA norm), yet it is applied to MI∫ outputs that live in the GROUP SU_q(2) (per the proof sibling eq:mi-decomp 'product is in the group'). Algebra-norm vs group-element-norm is conflated; this ambiguity is what enables the L2→L1 slip.

da-physical-implausibility.notes: Decomposing vortex mass into descended + transient parts is physically sensible; the issue is mathematical (L1 vs L2), not a physics/units violation.

da-referee-verdict.notes: VERDICT: reject-as-stated / major-revision. referee_argument: The lemma asserts a LINEAR sum-of-norms decomposition m(ϱ) = ‖MI∫τ̂ₙα‖ + ‖MI∫(α−τ̂ₙα)‖, but every supporting ingredient delivers something else: Killing-form orthogonality gives the Pythagorean L2 identity ‖α‖²=‖τ̂ₙα‖²+‖α−τ̂ₙα‖² (so m=√(‖A‖²+‖B‖²), not ‖A‖+‖B‖), and Yekutieli's nonabelian multiplicative integral is MULTIPLICATIVE (a product, as the proof's own eq:mi-decomp writes), not additive. The 'submultiplicativity is an equality for an idempotent' parenthetical is the unjustified leap. Compounding this, the Lean sibling tm_eigenspace_decomp proves only the trivial x = τ̂ₙx + (x−τ̂ₙx) (a simp tautology valid for any map), so the formalization does NOT back the lemma's substantive normed claim. Either restate as a Pythagorean (L2) identity and formalize the orthogonality genuinely, or supply the missing lemma making ‖A‖+‖B‖ correct (e.g. A,B non-negative scalars / colinear).
